questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Has she completed the record?

options.text: Has the record been completed by her?
Has the record completed by her?
Has the record had been completed by her?
Has the record been complete by her?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Has the record been completed by her?'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it to Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is **'**she**'**.
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the record'.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• 'has completed' will be changed into 'has been completed'.
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be used.
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Has the record been completed by her?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

I'll try to phone you __in the meeting.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. 'During the meeting'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3 is the correct answer because it uses the preposition "during" to convey the intended meaning that the action of phoning will take place while the meeting is ongoing. 
 
• **"During"** is the **appropriate **preposition to indicate an action happening within a specific time frame. 
 
• This option provides **a clear and accurate expression **of the intended meaning.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'I'll try to phone you during the meeting'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Explanation of why the other options are incorrect:**
 
• **At the meeting -** This option is not the best substitution as it does not capture the timing aspect of the action. "At the meeting" indicates the location or presence of someone during the meeting, rather than the action happening during that time.
 
• **In meeting - **This option is grammatically incorrect as it lacks the article "the" before "meeting." The correct phrase should be "in the meeting" rather than "in meeting." Using "in meeting" would be considered incomplete and improper English.

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Farah said to her aunt, “I am studying contemporary art.”

options.text: Farah told her aunt that she was study contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she is studying contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she had been studying contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art**.'

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question, we have to change it to Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• In the given sentence the reporting verb has an object. Hence, 'said to' will be changed into 'told'. 
 
• Commas and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• The conjunction 'that' will be added.
 
• 'I' will be changed into 'she' because the first-person pronoun**s** are changed according to the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• Present Continuous Tense 'am **studying**' will be changed into Past Continuous Tense 'was **studying**'.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The last man standing was ___________ a fully paid vacation to Las Vegas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. **'rewarded'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is: **'rewarded'**
 
• **In this context,** the phrase *"the last man standing" *typically refers to the winner of a competition or the survivor of a difficult or challenging situation.
 
• The reward for their efforts or success is typically something positive, such as a fully paid vacation to Las Vegas.
 
• Therefore, the word** "rewarded"** is most appropriate in this context.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'The last man standing was **rewarded** a fully paid vacation to Las Vegas.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **"Appreciated"** would imply that the person was shown gratitude or recognition, but this doesn't clearly imply a tangible reward such as a vacation.
 
• **"Discarded"** implies that the person was dismissed or thrown away, which doesn't make sense as a response to being the last man standing.
 
• **"Allotted"** could mean assigned or distributed, but it doesn't have the same connotation of earning or winning something as the word "rewarded" does.

questions.question:
**Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.**

Obfuscate
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Clarify.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer for the word opposite in meaning to "**Obfuscate**" is: **Clarify**.
 
• The word "**Obfuscate**" means** to make something unclear, confusing, or hard to understand.** (अंधेरा करना)It involves intentionally obscuring or muddling information or ideas.
 
 
• For example: The politician tried to **obfuscate **the issue by giving vague and contradictory statements.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**Clarify**" is the opposite of "**Obfuscate**." It means** to make something clear, understandable, or unambiguous.** (स्पष्ट करना) When you clarify something, you provide explanations, details, or examples to make it easier to comprehend.
 
 
• For instance: The teacher **clarified **the instructions, ensuring that the students understood the assignment.
 
 
 
• To summarize, the correct opposite for "**Obfuscate**" is "**Clarify**," as it denotes the act of making something clear and understandable. The other options, "Bid," "Mend," and "Languish," do not accurately represent the opposite meaning of "Obfuscate" but rather carry different meanings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **Bid**: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Obfuscate." "Bid" refers to making an offer, especially in an auction or competitive situation.(बोली) It does not carry an opposite meaning in relation to "Obfuscate."
 
• **Mend**: This option is not the correct opposite of "Obfuscate." "Mend" means to repair, fix, or improve something that is broken or damaged.(सुधार) It does not convey the opposite idea of making something clear or understandable.
 
• **Languish**: This option does not accurately represent the opposite meaning of "Obfuscate." "Languish" means to suffer or deteriorate, often due to neglect, lack of attention, or inactivity.(दुर्बल) It does not convey the opposite idea of making something clear or understandable.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The evil king was defeated by Gandolf, the savior.

options.text: Gandolf, the savior, defeated the evil king.
The savior of Gandolf defeated the evil king.
Gandolf, the savior, had defeated the evil king.
Gandolf, the savior, defeats the evil king.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. 'Gandolf, the savior, defeated the evil king.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**. We have to change the sentence into the** active form. **
 
• The given sentence is written in 'simple past tense' form. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Passive Voice: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
 
• Active Voice: Subject + V2 + Object.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Passive voice: Football was played by them.
 
• Active voice: They played football.
 
 
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'The evil king' and the subject of the given sentence is 'Gandolf, the savior.'
 
• So, in the active voice, the position of ‘object’ and ‘subject’ will be interchanged and 'by' will be removed. 
 
• Also here, 'was defeated' will be changed into 'defeated.'

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Gandolf, the savior, defeated the evil king.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Fiona enquired whether I had gone to school on Tuesday

options.text: “Had you been going to school on Tuesday?” Fiona asked me.
“Where are you going on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Are you gone to school on Tuesday? Fiona enquired.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is enquiring about something. So, the Direct Speech of this sentence must be an interrogative sentence.
 
• The rule of changing an indirect speech into a direct speech of an Interrogative sentence is as follows:
 
 
• In Indirect Narration, interrogative Verbs such as **“ask”, “enquire”, “demand”, “want to know”** etc are used as Reporting Verbs before the Reported Speech in place of simple Verb **“say” or “tell”**.
 
• **E.g.**__- He said to me, "Are you ill?" **(Direct Speech)**
 
• He **asked** (or **enquired of**) me if (or whether) I was ill. **(Indirect Speech)**
 
• If the Reported Speech in Direct Narration is introduced by Verbs like **“ be”, “have”, “do”, or any other auxiliary Verbs like “can”, “shall”, “will”**, the connective **“ if ”, “ whether ”** is used after the Reporting Verb or object of the Reporting verb in the Indirect Narration.
 
• __**E.g.**__- He said to me, "Are you ill?" **(Direct Speech)**
 
• He asked (or enquired of) me **if** (or **whether**) I was ill. **(Indirect Speech)**** **
 
 

 Hence, the correct answer is **“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Direct & Indirect Speech?**

 
 
• **Direct speech** – reporting the message of the speaker in the exact words as spoken by him.
 
• **Direct speech example:** Maya said, "I am busy now."
 
• **Indirect speech **– reporting the message of the speaker in our own words.
 
• **Indirect speech example:** Maya said that she was busy then.
